The corrupted element is most likely **Rz**. Its value (930 Ω) is well below 1/gm7, which is typically several kΩ for M7 at these bias levels. That leaves a right-half-plane zero near gm7/Cc, roughly 6–7 MHz. The zero adds gain and phase lag above the intended crossover, which fits the symptoms: f_unity pushed to 22.9 MHz and a shallow −14.8 dB/dec slope instead of the ideal −20.

Two checks support this over the other candidates. The DC gain of 20.66 dB matches −Rl/R1 (≈20.8 dB), so R1 and Rl look intact. The integrator's ideal unity frequency with Cf = 2.814 pF is about 4.2 MHz, which is near the target band, so Cf is not the main problem. Cc is the second suspect because it sets the compensation pole and zero together with Rz. M7 is a weaker third suspect since its gm sets the zero location.
